question: 44 + 78 − 62 + (35 + 16) × 2 − 81 = ?
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 4 i.e. 81.

GIVEN

• 44 + 78 − 62 + (35 + 16) × 2 − 81

SOLUTION

• Brackets first: (35 + 16) = 51.

• Multiply: 51 × 2 = 102.

• Now add/subtract left to right: 44 + 78 − 62 + 102 − 81 = 122 − 62 + 102 − 81 = 60 + 102 − 81 = 162 − 81 = 81.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 4.

SHORT TRICK

• Group the additions and subtractions separately: (44 + 78 + 102) − (62 + 81) = 224 − 143 = 81. Fast and error‑free.

NOTE

• Always follow BODMAS/PEMDAS: Brackets → Of/Orders → Division/Multiplication → Addition/Subtraction (left to right).

question: 65 − 27 + 39 ÷ 3 + (24 of 2) − 13 + 19 = ?
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 2 i.e. 105.

GIVEN

• 65 − 27 + 39 ÷ 3 + (24 of 2) − 13 + 19

SOLUTION

• 'of' and '÷' first: 24 of 2 = 48 and 39 ÷ 3 = 13.

• Expression = 65 − 27 + 13 + 48 − 13 + 19.

• = 38 + 13 + 48 − 13 + 19 = 51 + 48 − 13 + 19 = 99 − 13 + 19 = 86 + 19 = 105.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 2.

SHORT TRICK

• The +13 and −13 cancel out. Left with 65 − 27 + 48 + 19 = 105 instantly.

NOTE

• 'a of b' means a × b and ranks with multiplication in the BODMAS order.

question:
The pie chart given below shows the number of keys manufactured by 5 machines. The data is presented in the terms of degrees.

Average number of keys manufactured by M3 and M5 = 1500.

Number of keys manufactured by which machine are '2400'?
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 3 i.e. M2.

GIVEN

• Degrees: M1 = 54°, M2 = 120°, M3 = 72°, M4 = 36°, M5 = 78°; average of M3 and M5 = 1500.

SOLUTION

• M3 + M5 (keys) = 2 × 1500 = 3000, and their angle = 72° + 78° = 150°.

• So 150° ↔ 3000 keys ⇒ 1° ↔ 20 keys.

• 2400 keys ↔ 2400 ÷ 20 = 120°, which is M2.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 3.

SHORT TRICK

• Value per degree = 3000 ÷ 150 = 20. Divide the target 2400 by 20 to get 120° and match the slice directly.

NOTE

• In a degree pie chart, keys per degree = total keys ÷ 360; here total = 360 × 20 = 7200.

question:
The bar graph given below shows the per annum rate of interest offered on the 5 given simple interest investment schemes.

Simple Interest = [(Principal × Annual Rate of Interest × Time period)/100]

Principal in scheme R is Rs. X. Time period of investment in scheme R is 3 years. What is the simple interest (in Rs.) in scheme R?
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 1 i.e. X × 0.24.

GIVEN

• Rate for scheme R = 8% p.a., Principal = X, Time = 3 years.

SOLUTION

• SI = (P × R × T)/100 = (X × 8 × 3)/100.

• = 24X/100 = X × 0.24.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 1.

SHORT TRICK

• Just multiply rate × time = 8 × 3 = 24, put as a percent: 24% of X = X × 0.24.

NOTE

• SI grows linearly; (R × T)% of principal directly gives the interest — no year‑by‑year work needed.

question: A and B can do a piece of work in 12 days and 18 days, respectively. They work on alternate days, starting with A. How many days will it take to complete the work?
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 2 i.e. 14(1/3) days.

GIVEN

• A finishes in 12 days, B in 18 days; they work on alternate days starting with A.

SOLUTION

• Take total work = LCM(12, 18) = 36 units. A does 3 units/day, B does 2 units/day.

• One pair (A then B) = 2 days = 5 units. After 7 pairs = 14 days, work done = 35 units, 1 unit left.

• Day 15 is A's turn (3 units/day); 1 unit needs 1/3 day. Total = 14 + 1/3 = 14(1/3) days.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 2.

SHORT TRICK

• Per 2‑day cycle = 5 units. 36 ÷ 5 = 7 cycles (35 units) + 1 unit; the leftover falls on A ⇒ 14 + 1/3 days.

NOTE

• In alternate‑day problems, complete as many full 2‑day cycles as possible, then finish the remainder with whoever's turn is next.

question: 300 kg of rice was purchased at the rate of ₹20 per kg and sold at a profit of 5%. Compute the profit and the selling price per kg.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 1 i.e. ₹300, ₹21.

GIVEN

• 300 kg at ₹20/kg, sold at 5% profit.

SOLUTION

• Cost price = 300 × 20 = ₹6000.

• Profit = 5% of 6000 = ₹300; total SP = 6000 + 300 = ₹6300.

• SP per kg = 6300 ÷ 300 = ₹21, profit = ₹300.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 1.

SHORT TRICK

• SP per kg = CP per kg × 1.05 = 20 × 1.05 = ₹21; profit = 5% of total cost = ₹300.

NOTE

• Selling price = Cost price × (1 + profit%/100). A 5% rise on ₹20 adds just ₹1.

question: If x% of y equals 1500 and simultaneously y% of z equals 2000, establish the algebraic relationship connecting x and z.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 2 i.e. 4x = 3z.

GIVEN

• x% of y = 1500 and y% of z = 2000.

SOLUTION

• xy/100 = 1500 and yz/100 = 2000.

• Divide the first by the second: (xy)/(yz) = 1500/2000 ⇒ x/z = 3/4.

• Cross‑multiplying: 4x = 3z.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 2.

SHORT TRICK

• 'a% of b' = 'b% of a', so x% of y ÷ y% of z gives x : z = 1500 : 2000 = 3 : 4 ⇒ 4x = 3z.

NOTE

• Dividing two equations that share a common variable (here y) eliminates it instantly.

question: A student borrowed ₹6,400 from his teacher at 7.5% simple interest per annum. He repaid the money after 3 years, along with an additional club membership fee of ₹360. Find the total amount he paid back.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 3 i.e. ₹8,200.

GIVEN

• Principal = ₹6400, Rate = 7.5% p.a., Time = 3 years, extra fee = ₹360.

SOLUTION

• SI = (6400 × 7.5 × 3)/100 = (6400 × 22.5)/100 = ₹1440.

• Amount = 6400 + 1440 = ₹7840; add fee ₹360.

• Total = 7840 + 360 = ₹8200.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 3.

SHORT TRICK

• 7.5% × 3 = 22.5% of 6400 = ₹1440. Then 6400 + 1440 + 360 = ₹8200.

NOTE

• Total repayment = Principal + Simple Interest + any fixed charges; don't forget flat add‑ons like the fee.

question: A number is split into two unequal parts. The difference of the squares of the two parts is 84 times the difference of the two parts. What is the number?
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 4 i.e. 84.

GIVEN

• A number N = a + b (a ≠ b) with a² − b² = 84 × (a − b).

SOLUTION

• a² − b² = (a + b)(a − b).

• So (a + b)(a − b) = 84(a − b); since a ≠ b, cancel (a − b).

• a + b = 84, and the number = a + b = 84.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 4.

SHORT TRICK

• Difference of squares ÷ difference of parts = sum of parts = the number itself = 84.

NOTE

• Key identity: a² − b² = (a + b)(a − b); the ratio (a²−b²)/(a−b) always equals (a + b).

question: The average of 20 balls is 33. If the value of each ball is increased by 6, what will the new average be?
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 3 i.e. 39.

GIVEN

• Average of 20 balls = 33; each value increased by 6.

SOLUTION

• When every observation increases by the same amount, the average increases by that amount.

• New average = 33 + 6 = 39.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 3.

SHORT TRICK

• Add the constant increment straight to the mean: 33 + 6 = 39. The count (20) is irrelevant.

NOTE

• Adding k to each value shifts the mean by k; multiplying each value by k multiplies the mean by k.

question: A shopkeeper marks a mobile phone 30% above its cost price. During a festival sale, he offers two successive discounts of 10% and 5% on the marked price. If his cost price is Rs. 12000, find the selling price of the mobile phone and the profit earned.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 3 i.e. SP is Rs.13338, Profit is 1338.

GIVEN

• CP = Rs. 12000, mark‑up 30%, successive discounts 10% and 5%.

SOLUTION

• Marked price = 12000 × 1.30 = Rs. 15600.

• After 10% off: 15600 × 0.90 = Rs. 14040. After 5% off: 14040 × 0.95 = Rs. 13338.

• Profit = 13338 − 12000 = Rs. 1338; SP = Rs. 13338.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 3.

SHORT TRICK

• Net factor = 1.30 × 0.90 × 0.95 = 1.11135; × 12000 = Rs. 13338 in one shot.

NOTE

• Successive discounts of a% and b% combine to a single factor (1−a/100)(1−b/100); order does not matter.

question: Find the smallest number by which 640 must be multiplied so that the product becomes a perfect square. Also, find the square root of the resulting number.
option_1: - Multiply by: 8  - Resulting perfect square: 5120  - Square root: 71
option_2: - Multiply by: 4  - Resulting perfect square: 2560  - Square root: 50
option_3: - Multiply by: 5  - Resulting perfect square: 3250  - Square root: 56
option_4: - Multiply by: 10  - Resulting perfect square: 6400  - Square root: 80
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 4 i.e. - Multiply by: 10  - Resulting perfect square: 6400  - Square root: 80.

GIVEN

• Number 640 to be made a perfect square by smallest multiplication.

SOLUTION

• Prime factorise: 640 = 2⁷ × 5.

• For a perfect square all exponents must be even; 2⁷ needs one more 2 and 5¹ needs one more 5 ⇒ multiply by 2 × 5 = 10.

• Product = 640 × 10 = 6400 = 2⁸ × 5², √6400 = 80.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 4.

SHORT TRICK

• Multiply the odd‑power primes once each: 2 (for 2⁷) and 5 (for 5¹) → factor 10. √6400 = 80 since 80² = 6400.

NOTE

• A number is a perfect square iff every prime factor appears an even number of times.

question: A postal runner on foot leaves Post Office A at 6:00 a.m. toward Post Office B at a steady speed of 6 km/h. A scooter departs from Post Office B toward A at 7:30 a.m. at a speed of 42 km/h. The distance between A and B is 210 km. At what clock time will they meet? (Round minutes and seconds to the nearest second)
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 2 i.e. 11:41:15 a.m..

GIVEN

• Runner: 6 km/h from A at 6:00; Scooter: 42 km/h from B at 7:30; distance = 210 km.

SOLUTION

• Head start of runner (6:00 to 7:30 = 1.5 h): 6 × 1.5 = 9 km. Remaining gap = 210 − 9 = 201 km.

• Closing speed = 6 + 42 = 48 km/h; time = 201 ÷ 48 = 4.1875 h = 4 h 11 min 15 s.

• From 7:30 a.m. add 4 h 11 min 15 s ⇒ meet at 11:41:15 a.m.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 2.

SHORT TRICK

• Subtract the head‑start distance first, then divide the leftover by the combined speed: 201/48 h; 0.1875 h × 60 = 11.25 min = 11 min 15 s.

NOTE

• For objects moving toward each other, time to meet = remaining distance ÷ (sum of speeds).

question: The area of a rectangle is 60 square cm. The length of the rectangle is 10 cm. What is the ratio of length and breadth of the rectangle?
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 1 i.e. 5 : 3.

GIVEN

• Area = 60 cm², length = 10 cm.

SOLUTION

• Breadth = Area ÷ Length = 60 ÷ 10 = 6 cm.

• Length : Breadth = 10 : 6 = 5 : 3.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 1.

SHORT TRICK

• Ratio = length² : area = 100 : 60 = 5 : 3 (since breadth = area/length).

NOTE

• For a rectangle, breadth = area ÷ length; simplify the resulting ratio by the common factor.

question: The length of a rectangle is 24 cm. The diagonal of the rectangle is 30 cm. What is the area (in square cm) of the rectangle?
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 3 i.e. 432.

GIVEN

• Length = 24 cm, diagonal = 30 cm.

SOLUTION

• Breadth = √(diagonal² − length²) = √(30² − 24²) = √(900 − 576) = √324 = 18 cm.

• Area = length × breadth = 24 × 18 = 432 cm².

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 3.

SHORT TRICK

• Recognise the 24‑18‑30 triangle as a 4‑3‑5 triple × 6, so breadth = 18 instantly; area = 24 × 18 = 432.

NOTE

• In a rectangle, length² + breadth² = diagonal² (Pythagoras on the diagonal).

question:
In the given figure, what is the value (in degrees) of (x + y + z)?

[Figure: Straight line B–C–D (extended beyond D). A is the apex. AB, AC and AD are drawn; ∠BAC = x and ∠CAD = y at A, ∠ABC = z at B. At C the marked angle ∠ACD = 105°; at D the marked (exterior) angle = 125°.]
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 1 i.e. 125.

GIVEN

• B, C, D collinear; ∠ACD = 105° (exterior angle of △ABC at C) and the exterior angle at D = 125°.

SOLUTION

• Exterior angle of △ABC at C = x + z ⇒ x + z = 105°.

• Exterior angle of △ACD at D = ∠CAD + ∠ACD ⇒ 125° = y + 105° ⇒ y = 20°.

• Therefore x + y + z = (x + z) + y = 105° + 20° = 125°.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 1.

SHORT TRICK

• The exterior angle at the far vertex (D = 125°) already equals x + y + z, since it is the exterior angle of the whole triangle A–B–D at D.

NOTE

• Exterior‑angle theorem: an exterior angle of a triangle equals the sum of the two remote interior angles.

question: What is the Highest Common Factor of 16/45, 24/60 and 32/75?
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 1 i.e. 2/225.

GIVEN

• Fractions 16/45, 24/60 and 32/75.

SOLUTION

• HCF of fractions = HCF(numerators) ÷ LCM(denominators).

• HCF(16, 24, 32) = 8. LCM(45, 60, 75): 45 = 3²·5, 60 = 2²·3·5, 75 = 3·5² ⇒ LCM = 2²·3²·5² = 900.

• HCF = 8/900 = 2/225.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 1.

SHORT TRICK

• Numerator HCF over denominator LCM, then reduce: 8/900 ÷ 4 = 2/225.

NOTE

• HCF of fractions = HCF of numerators / LCM of denominators; always simplify the final fraction. (Option 3 '8/900' is the un‑reduced form.)

question: There is a rectangular floor of size 336 cm × 420 cm. The floor is to tiled with largest square tiles. How many such tiles will be required?
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 3 i.e. 20.

GIVEN

• Rectangular floor 336 cm × 420 cm, tiled with largest possible square tiles.

SOLUTION

• Largest square side = HCF(336, 420) = 84 cm (336 = 2⁴·3·7, 420 = 2²·3·5·7 ⇒ HCF = 2²·3·7 = 84).

• Tiles along length = 420 ÷ 84 = 5; along breadth = 336 ÷ 84 = 4.

• Number of tiles = 5 × 4 = 20.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 3.

SHORT TRICK

• Tiles = (Area of floor) ÷ (side²) = (336 × 420) ÷ 84² = (336/84) × (420/84) = 4 × 5 = 20.

NOTE

• Largest square tile side = HCF of the two dimensions; count = product of the two quotients.

question:
In the given figure, AB is parallel to CD. PQ = QR. Angle BQS = 72 degrees. What is the value (in degrees) of angle PRQ?

[Figure: AB and CD are horizontal parallel lines. A straight transversal S–Q–P–T cuts AB at Q and CD at P. Another segment joins Q to R on CD (R between P and D), with PQ = QR. ∠BQS = 72°.]
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 1 i.e. 72.

GIVEN

• AB ∥ CD, PQ = QR, ∠BQS = 72°.

SOLUTION

• ∠PQB = 180° − ∠BQS = 180° − 72° = 108° (angles on line SQP at Q).

• AB ∥ CD ⇒ co‑interior angles: ∠QPD = 180° − ∠PQB = 180° − 108° = 72°, so ∠QPR = 72°.

• PQ = QR ⇒ △PQR isosceles ⇒ ∠PRQ = ∠QPR = 72°.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 1.

SHORT TRICK

• ∠BQS = 72° equals its alternate angle ∠QPR (via the parallel lines) = 72°; equal sides PQ = QR make ∠PRQ equal to it.

NOTE

• Angles opposite equal sides of a triangle are equal (isosceles‑triangle property); combine with parallel‑line angle rules.

question: A car travels from A to B at the speed of 40 km/hr and travels from B to A at speed of 60 km/hr. What is the average speed (in km/hr) of the car?
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 2 i.e. 48.

GIVEN

• Speed A→B = 40 km/hr, B→A = 60 km/hr (equal distances).

SOLUTION

• For equal distances, average speed = harmonic mean = 2ab/(a + b).

• = (2 × 40 × 60)/(40 + 60) = 4800/100 = 48 km/hr.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 2.

SHORT TRICK

• Same distance both ways ⇒ use 2ab/(a+b): (2·40·60)/100 = 48. Never the simple average (50).

NOTE

• Average speed = total distance ÷ total time; for two equal legs it is the harmonic mean of the two speeds, always below the arithmetic mean.
